key_evidence_accepted: The Supreme Court accepted that the allegations in the FIRs are distinct and separate, and may be regarded as counter complaints, thus allowing the registration of the second FIR.
witness_credibility: The court assessed the main witnesses by noting that the allegations made by the accused in the first FIR alleging a different version of the same incident were permissible and did not constitute an improvement of the facts mentioned in the original complaint.

legal_representation.accused: Nagendra Rai, R.K. Dash, Altaf Ahmed, Smarhar Singh, Shantanu Sagar, Abhishek Kr. singh, Gopi Raman, Chandra Prakash, Abhisth Kumar, Archana Singh, Ashok K. Srivasta
legal_representation.state: Mr. R.K. Dash, learned senior counsel for the State

prosecution_argument: The prosecution argued that the registration of a second FIR relating to the same incident is prohibited under the Code of Criminal Procedure, as it would amount to an improvement of the facts mentioned in the original complaint and would hinder the investigation.
defence_argument: The defence argued that the second FIR is permissible as it involves distinct and separate allegations, different accused persons, and different versions of the same incident, which do not fall under the principle of sameness.
legal_principle_applied: The Supreme Court applied the principle that the lodgment of two FIRs is not permissible in respect of one and the same incident, but the concept of sameness does not encompass filing of a counter FIR relating to the same or connected cognizable offence.
